role: sha256 of go2.sh, the script of control I, written at launch.
purpose: The file holds one line: the sha256 checksum of the local file go2.sh, the script of control I. The facts sheet calls it "written at launch", and build_facts.py later tested go2.sh against it (check 20 of the facts sheet).

main_flow.step: Read the line as: checksum (64 hexadecimal digits, 256 bits), two spaces, file name. The name has no folder part. It names go2.sh in the folder of go2.sha.

The checksum of go2.sh is not in local.sha. local.sha has the file time 22:12:03. go2.sh has the file time 22:23:30, 687 s later (2026-11-17 UTC, clock of the agent's server). The facts sheet says that control I was added after the first numbers of parts A, L and C were seen (decision (g)) [Ref3].

The agent wrote go2.sh and then this file in one command line. The part that wrote this file is `sha256sum go2.sh > go2.sha`. The same command line copied both files to the folder `~/cache-perf/w120-7200-20261117` on CRB and ran `sha256sum -c go2.sha` there. The output shows `go2.sh: OK` [Ref6].
To test go2.sh against the line, run `sha256sum -c go2.sha` in this folder. On 2026-11-21 it printed `go2.sh: OK` (run for this page).

build_facts.py reads this line together with the 5 lines of local.sha and reports the test as check 20 of the facts sheet. The facts sheet in this folder was built before line 20 of go.sh was edited on 2026-11-24. It says: pass, 6 files equal [Ref1] [Ref3].
go2.sha has the file time 22:23:30, less than 1 s after the file time of go2.sh. go2.sh started on CRB at 22:23:35 by the clock of CRB. The two clocks were not compared [Ref3].

The session record holds both steps with times of one clock, the clock of the agent's server. The command line that wrote go2.sh and go2.sha was sent at 22:23:30 UTC. The command that started go2.sh was sent at 22:23:35 UTC [Ref6].
facts_text.py lists the file as Ref16 of the facts sheet with the words "sha256 of go2.sh, written at launch" [Ref2].

behavior_notes: **What the line allows.** A reader can test whether go2.sh still has the content that it had when go2.sha was written (file time 22:23:30 UTC on 2026-11-17). When go2.sh was changed later, `sha256sum -c` and check 20 fail. Check 20 also tests the 5 files of local.sha. Since 2026-11-24 a new run of build_facts.py fails check 20 because of go.sh. Line 20 of go.sh was edited on that day. The page `go.sh.md` in this folder (the explanation of go.sh) gives the proof. `sha256sum -c go2.sha` still prints `go2.sh: OK` (tested on 2026-11-24).

**The copy on CRB.** The command `sha256sum -c go2.sha` on CRB printed `go2.sh: OK` about 5 s before go2.sh was started. The session record holds no command of the agent between this test and the start of go2.sh [Ref6]. The 2 logs, the 3 probe.txt files and the 9 env.txt files of the rerun hold no checksum of go2.sh (limit stated in check 26 of the facts sheet) [Ref3]. Check 20 tests the local copy only.

**What the records of CRB do show.** The log of go2.sh ends with ALLDONE and holds no line that starts with FAILED (check 2 of the facts sheet) [Ref3]. go2.sh tests the sha256 of rx.sh and of bwx12 on CRB before the first measurement, with the same two values as go.sh [Ref5] [Ref4].
**Who wrote the file.** The agent wrote it. The session record holds the command: `sha256sum go2.sh > go2.sha`, run in this folder [Ref6]. The facts sheet calls the file "written at launch" [Ref3].

words.def: a checksum. Two files with the same sha256 have the same content.
the Linux tool that prints the sha256 of a file. With the option `-c` it reads a list such as this file and tests every named file against its checksum.
the Arm reference server under test. It has 128 CPUs.
million transfers per second, the unit of memory speed.
the whole-chip read test of 2026-11-17 at 7200 MT/s.
the scripts and spec files of the rerun in this folder: go.sh, ra.sh, like.spec, cfwd.spec, crev.spec, and go2.sh, which was added later.
the AI coding assistant (Claude Code) that ran the rerun on CRB for the user. FACTS.md calls it "the agent".
the agent's server is the machine that holds this folder. The local copy of a run file is the file in this folder. CRB held its own copies under `~/cache-perf/w120-7200-20261117`.

the record of the Claude Code session of 2026-11-17 in which the agent ran the rerun. It is a file with one JSON record per line. It holds the commands that the agent ran and their output. The times in it are from the clock of the agent's server. The file lies outside the project folder.
the inner loop of the benchmark that reads memory. On this page "kernel" means this loop. The operating system kernel is always written "Linux kernel".
the benchmark and its two binaries of 2026-11-13. bw_old was built from the old source, bw_new from the new source.
later runner programs for the same loops. They print one row per thread. bwx12 is the runner of the 2026-11-15 investigation. bwx11 and bwx are older versions.

a process is one start of a benchmark binary. An interval is one timed measurement inside a process. bwx12 times a sequence of kernels and repeats the sequence: each repeat is a round (counted from 0), and the position is the place of a kernel in the sequence (counted from 0). In part A the round (1 or 2) is the round of the script: round 2 runs the processes in the reverse order.
one pass of go.sh through part A, part L and part C.
the 120-thread part of the test of 2026-11-13, repeated with the same two binaries.
one bwx12 process with the kernel sequence oldread, asmread, read_nop96, read_nop256, read_1pl.
one bwx12 process with the sequence oldread, read, asmread (cfwd) or asmread, read, oldread (crev).
the part L line, started from an idle machine, twice. It was added after the first numbers were seen. It is not part of the plan fixed before the run.
the driver script of the rerun: three sessions of parts A, L, C and a fourth part C process.
the script of part A.
the script of control I: the part L line twice, each time from an idle machine.
the runner script of the bwx12 processes (parts L, C, I). It reads a spec file and starts one process per line.
a text file for rx.sh. Each line has the form `tag|arguments` and starts one process. like.spec, cfwd.spec and crev.spec hold one line each.
the file FACTS.md in this folder. The script build_facts.py wrote it from the raw files. It is the source of the report of the rerun.
numbered integrity checks in section 1.4 of the facts sheet. build_facts.py runs them and writes one line per check.
baselines-and-rules.txt in this folder: the list of the 8000 MT/s baselines and the comparison rules, written before the run.
a file that ra.sh writes on CRB at the start of part A. It holds the time, the load, the boot id, and the sha256 of bw_old, bw_new and ra.sh.
a random identifier that Linux creates at each start. Equal boot ids mean the same boot.
rx.sh writes one launch line per process into launches.txt on CRB. The line holds the tag and the arguments of the process.
a file that rx.sh writes on CRB when it starts. It holds the date, the Linux kernel release, the load, the logins, the busiest processes, and the path and the sha256 of the binary.
the saved output of go.sh and of go2.sh: the files go-T72-20261117T221209Z.log and go2-T72-20261117T222335Z.log in the results folder.
